recipes.title: Steamed Sona Masoori Rice
recipes.description: Soft, separate grains of everyday sona masoori rice, cooked in a pressure cooker or an open pot. The base for sambar, rasam, kootu and curries. One serving = about 1 cup cooked rice (70 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Put the rice in the pressure-cooker pan, cover with water and rub the grains gently between your fingers. Drain and repeat two or three times until the water runs almost clear. This removes surface starch so the grains stay separate.
steps.visual: Raw white sona masoori rice under cloudy rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan, a hand swirling the grains

steps.title: Soak briefly
steps.text: Drain the rice, add the 3 cups of measured water and leave it to soak for 20 minutes. Soaked rice cooks more evenly and needs less time on the stove.
steps.visual: Rinsed rice resting under clear water in the same steel pressure-cooker pan on the counter, the grains turned opaque white

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the cooker and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles, about 8 to 10 minutes, then turn off the heat. For an open pot, bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker with its lid locked on a medium gas flame, the whistle lifting with a puff of steam

steps.title: Let the pressure drop
steps.text: Leave the cooker undisturbed for 10 minutes until the pressure settles on its own. The rice finishes cooking in the trapped steam.
steps.visual: The closed pressure cooker sitting off the flame on the stove top, no steam escaping

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Open the lid and fluff the rice gently with a flat spoon, lifting from the bottom so the grains don't break. Serve hot with sambar, dal or a curry and a vegetable side.
steps.visual: Fluffy white rice with distinct grains in a steel serving bowl, a ladle of sambar and a small bowl of beans poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Brown rice needs a 30-minute soak and 4 to 5 whistles; it has more fibre per serving.
Foxtail millet cooks in 2 whistles with 2½ cups water per cup and has more fibre and protein than white rice.

recipes.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within an hour; use within 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with a tablespoon of water and microwave covered for 1 to 2 minutes, or steam until piping hot.

recipes.title: Kerala Matta Rice (Boiled and Drained)
recipes.description: Plump, nutty red matta rice cooked the Kerala way in plenty of water and then drained, which keeps the grains separate. Made for fish curry, sambar and thoran. One serving = about 1 cup cooked rice (70 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Wash the matta rice in a large bowl of water, rubbing the grains, and drain. Repeat twice; the water will stay slightly pink from the bran.
steps.visual: Reddish-brown matta rice grains in a steel bowl of pinkish rinse water, fingers rubbing the grains

steps.title: Soak for an hour
steps.text: Cover the rice with fresh water and soak for 1 hour. This cuts the boiling time by about 10 minutes and helps the thick grains cook through evenly.
steps.visual: Matta rice soaking under clear water in the same steel bowl, the grains slightly swollen

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring 8 cups of water to a rolling boil in a large, deep saucepan and add the salt.
steps.visual: A large, deep steel saucepan of water at a rolling boil on a high gas flame

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until a grain pressed between your fingers is soft with no hard centre. In a pressure cooker, use 5 cups water, cook for 5 to 6 whistles and then drain.
steps.visual: Plump red matta rice grains tumbling in bubbling, cloudy starch water in the deep steel saucepan, a wooden spoon resting across the rim

steps.title: Drain the starch water
steps.text: Hold the lid slightly ajar and pour off the starchy water (kanji vellam), or tip the rice into a colander. Keep the water to drink warm with a pinch of salt if you like.
steps.visual: Cloudy white starch water pouring from the tilted saucepan through a gap under the lid, the cooked red rice held back inside

steps.title: Rest covered
steps.text: Cover and leave for 5 minutes so the last of the moisture steams off and the grains firm up.
steps.visual: Drained matta rice steaming gently in the covered steel saucepan on the switched-off stove

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fluff with a spoon and serve hot with fish curry, sambar or moru curry and a vegetable thoran.
steps.visual: Fat, separate red matta rice grains on a banana leaf with a ladle of red fish curry and green cabbage thoran beside them

substitutions.note: Sona masoori cooks in a quarter of the time but has less fibre; use the absorption method instead of draining.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate in a closed box for up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Steam or microwave covered with a splash of water until hot right through.

recipes.title: Fluffy Pressure-Cooked Brown Rice
recipes.description: Chewy, nutty whole-grain rice with separate grains, using a soak and gentle pressure cooking so it is never hard in the centre. Pairs with dal, rajma or any curry. One serving = about 1 cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Rinse the brown rice in the pressure-cooker pan two or three times and drain well.
steps.visual: Light tan brown-rice grains under rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Add the 2½ cups of measured water and soak for 30 minutes. Brown rice keeps its bran layer, and soaking lets water reach the centre of the grain.
steps.visual: Brown rice soaking under clear water in the same steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Season the water
steps.text: Stir in the salt and the oil, if using. The oil helps keep the grains separate and reduces foaming in the cooker.
steps.visual: A few drops of oil glistening on the water above the soaked brown rice in the cooker pan, a spoon stirring in the salt

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 4 whistles, then lower the heat and cook 5 minutes more. In an open pot, use 3 cups water, cover and cook on low heat for 40 to 45 minutes.
steps.visual: The closed pressure cooker on a medium gas flame with steam puffing from the whistle

steps.title: Natural release
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own, about 15 minutes. Opening it early leaves the grains wet.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker resting off the heat on the stove top, the whistle settled

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork and serve with dal, rajma, or a chicken or paneer curry.
steps.visual: Separate, plump brown-rice grains piled in a ceramic bowl with steam rising, a bowl of rajma beside it

substitutions.note: Kerala matta rice is another whole-bran rice; boil it in plenty of water and drain instead.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; brown rice holds its texture well in lunch boxes.
recipes.reheating: Microwave covered with 1 tbsp water for 2 minutes, or stir in a hot pan until steaming.

recipes.title: Foxtail Millet (Thinai) Rice
recipes.description: Light, fluffy foxtail millet cooked by the absorption method in a covered pot, an everyday swap for rice with sambar, kuzhambu and poriyal. One serving = about ¾ cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Wash well
steps.text: Rinse the millet in a bowl 3 to 4 times, swishing well, as the tiny grains can hold dust and husk. Drain through a fine sieve.
steps.visual: Tiny pale-yellow foxtail millet grains in a steel bowl of cloudy water, a few husks floating on top

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover the millet with fresh water and soak for 30 minutes, then drain.
steps.visual: Foxtail millet soaking under clear water in the same steel bowl

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring the 2¼ cups of measured water to a boil in a heavy saucepan with the salt and the ghee, if using.
steps.visual: Water at a rolling boil in a heavy-bottomed steel saucepan, a little ghee shimmering on the surface

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Add the drained millet, stir once, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes until all the water is absorbed and small steam holes appear on the surface. In a pressure cooker, use 2 cups water and cook for 2 whistles.
steps.visual: Cooked foxtail millet in the uncovered steel saucepan, its surface dotted with small steam holes and no water left

steps.title: Rest and fluff
steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
steps.visual: Fluffed, separate millet grains in the saucepan with a fork lifting them

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with sambar, rasam or kuzhambu and a vegetable poriyal, just as you would serve rice.
steps.visual: A mound of fluffy pale-gold foxtail millet on a steel plate with sambar poured over one side and carrot poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Little millet (samai) cooks the same way with 2 cups water per cup and turns slightly softer.

recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and steam or microwave covered; millet dries out faster than rice.

recipes.title: Little Millet (Samai) Rice in a Pressure Cooker
recipes.description: Soft samai rice cooked with a short soak and two whistles. Its mild taste suits rasam, sambar, dry curries and curd. One serving = about ¾ cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the millet
steps.text: Wash the samai in the pressure-cooker pan 3 to 4 times, swirling well, and drain carefully through a fine sieve so no grains escape.
steps.visual: Tiny cream-coloured little-millet grains in cloudy rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Add the 2 cups of measured water and soak for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Little millet soaking under clear water in the same steel cooker pan

steps.title: Add salt and oil
steps.text: Stir in the salt and a few drops of sesame oil, if using, to keep the grains from clumping.
steps.visual: A spoon stirring salt into the water over the soaked millet, a few golden drops of sesame oil floating on top

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the cooker and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles, about 8 minutes, then turn off the heat.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker on a medium flame letting out its second whistle in a burst of steam

steps.title: Release and fluff
steps.text: Let the pressure drop naturally, about 10 minutes, then open and fluff the millet gently with a fork.
steps.visual: The opened cooker showing soft, fluffed little-millet rice with steam rising from it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with sambar, rasam or a dry curry, or cool it and mix with curd.
steps.visual: Soft samai rice in a brass bowl beside a small bowl of tomato rasam and a spoonful of beans poriyal

substitutions.note: Foxtail millet works the same way; add ¼ cup more water as it is slightly firmer.

recipes.reheating: Steam or microwave covered with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.title: Whole-Wheat Phulka
recipes.description: Thin, soft, puffed whole-wheat flatbreads cooked on a tawa and finished over the flame, with no oil in the dough. Makes 10 phulkas; one serving = 2 phulkas.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the atta and salt in a wide bowl. Add the water a little at a time, mixing with your fingers, until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
steps.visual: Soft, smooth light-brown wheat dough being kneaded with the knuckles in a wide steel mixing bowl, a little flour on the rim

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the bowl and rest the dough for 20 minutes. Resting relaxes the gluten so the phulkas roll thin without shrinking back.
steps.visual: The ball of dough covered with a damp cloth in the same steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Divide into balls
steps.text: Knead the dough briefly again and divide it into 10 equal balls of about 50 g each. Keep them covered while you work.
steps.visual: Ten smooth, equal dough balls lined up on a steel plate beside the empty mixing bowl

steps.title: Roll thin
steps.text: Dip a ball in the dusting flour and roll it into an even 6-inch circle, turning it as you roll. Even thickness is what makes a phulka puff.
steps.visual: A thin, round dough circle on a wooden rolling board with a rolling pin, a small plate of dusting flour beside it

steps.title: Cook on the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium-high heat. Place the rolled phulka on it and cook about 20 seconds until small bubbles appear, then flip and cook the other side for 30 to 40 seconds until light brown spots form.
steps.visual: A thin phulka on a hot black iron tawa, its surface dotted with small bubbles and pale brown spots

steps.title: Puff over the flame
steps.text: Lift the phulka with tongs and hold it, first-cooked side down, directly over the open flame for a few seconds until it balloons. Flip for 2 seconds. On an induction hob, press the edges gently with a folded cloth on the tawa instead.
steps.visual: A fully puffed, balloon-like phulka held with steel tongs over a blue gas flame, light brown spots on its surface

steps.title: Stack and serve
steps.text: Brush lightly with ghee if you like and stack in a cloth-lined box to keep soft while you roll and cook the rest. Serve warm with dal and a sabzi.
steps.visual: A stack of soft, brown-spotted phulkas in a cloth-lined steel box, the top one glistening with a little ghee, a bowl of dal beside it

substitutions.note: Jowar rotis are gluten-free but need hot water to bind and are patted rather than rolled; they puff less.

recipes.storage: Wrap in a cloth inside a closed box and eat the same day. The dough keeps 1 day refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a hot tawa for 10 seconds per side.

recipes.title: Bajra Roti (Pearl Millet Flatbread)
recipes.description: Rustic, earthy pearl-millet rotis from Rajasthan and Gujarat, patted out by hand and cooked on a tawa. Naturally gluten-free and best eaten hot. Makes 6 rotis; one serving = 2 rotis.

steps.title: Mix flour and salt
steps.text: Mix the bajra flour and salt in a wide bowl.
steps.visual: Grey-green bajra flour with a pinch of salt in a wide steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Knead in small batches
steps.text: Bajra has no gluten, so knead only enough for 2 rotis at a time. Take a third of the flour, add warm water a little at a time and knead with the heel of your palm for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth and free of cracks.
steps.visual: A smooth, soft grey dough ball being pressed with the heel of the palm on one side of the steel bowl, dry flour still heaped on the other side

steps.title: Pat out the rotis
steps.text: Divide into 2 balls. Dust with flour and pat each between your palms, or on a plastic sheet, into a 5-inch round about 3 mm thick. Smooth any cracking edges with a wet finger.
steps.visual: A round, slightly thick grey roti being patted out on a plastic sheet with wet fingertips, the edges smoothed

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium-high heat. Lay the roti on it and brush the top with a little water. Cook for about 1 minute until the underside has light spots.
steps.visual: A grey bajra roti on a black iron tawa, its top glistening with a thin film of water

steps.title: Flip and puff
steps.text: Flip, cook for 1 minute, then flip again and press gently with a folded cloth, or hold it over the flame, until it puffs in patches and has brown spots. Repeat with the remaining flour in batches.
steps.visual: A bajra roti over a gas flame, puffed in patches with dark brown spots across its surface

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Smear with a little ghee, if using, and serve hot with dal, a leafy sabzi or garlic chutney. Bajra rotis firm up as they cool.
steps.visual: Two hot, brown-spotted bajra rotis on a steel plate with a little ghee melting on top, a bowl of dal and a green sabzi beside them

substitutions.note: Jowar flour makes a softer, milder roti with the same method.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep 1 day wrapped in a cloth.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa with a sprinkle of water so they soften in the steam.

recipes.title: Soft Idli (Classic Fermented Batter)
recipes.description: Pillowy steamed idlis from a 4:1 idli rice and urad dal batter, ground and fermented overnight. Makes about 32 idlis; one serving = 4 idlis. Serve with sambar and chutney.

steps.title: Soak rice and dal
steps.text: Wash the idli rice 3 times and soak it in plenty of water in one bowl. In a second bowl wash the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds and soak them together. Soak both for 5 hours.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls on the counter: one of plump, opaque parboiled rice under water, the other of white split urad dal with a few yellow fenugreek seeds

steps.title: Grind the urad dal
steps.text: Drain the dal and grind it in a mixer or wet grinder, sprinkling in cold water a few tablespoons at a time, for 8 to 10 minutes until very smooth, fluffy and nearly doubled. A spoonful dropped into water should float.
steps.visual: Bright white, fluffy, mousse-like urad dal batter clinging to the sides of a mixer jar, a spoonful floating in a small cup of water beside it

steps.title: Grind the rice
steps.text: Transfer the dal batter to a large bowl. Drain the rice and grind it with just enough water to a slightly coarse batter, like fine semolina. Pour it over the dal batter.
steps.visual: A large steel mixing bowl of fluffy white dal batter with slightly grainy rice batter being poured over it from the mixer jar

steps.title: Mix with salt
steps.text: Add the salt and mix the two batters with your hand for a minute; the warmth of your hand helps fermentation. The batter should be thick but pourable.
steps.visual: A hand folding the combined thick, creamy-white idli batter in the large steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Ferment overnight
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave in a warm spot for 8 to 12 hours until the batter rises, looks bubbly and smells pleasantly sour. In cold weather, keep it inside a switched-off oven with the light on.
steps.visual: The same steel bowl the next morning, the batter risen almost to the rim with a domed surface full of tiny bubbles

steps.title: Grease the moulds
steps.text: Stir the batter gently without beating out the air. Grease the idli plates lightly with oil, pour 2 cups of water into the steamer or pressure-cooker base and bring it to a boil.
steps.visual: Lightly oiled steel idli plates stacked beside the bowl of bubbly batter, a pot of boiling water steaming behind them

steps.title: Fill and steam
steps.text: Fill each mould three-quarters full. Place the stand in the steamer, cover (remove the whistle if using a pressure cooker) and steam on medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
steps.visual: Idli moulds filled three-quarters with white batter on an idli stand being lowered into a steaming pot

steps.title: Rest and unmould
steps.text: Lift out the stand and leave it for 2 minutes, then run a wet spoon around each idli and lift it out.
steps.visual: Puffed, glossy white idlis in the steel idli plates, one being scooped out with a wet spoon

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with sambar and coconut or tomato chutney. Steam the remaining batter in batches as needed.
steps.visual: Four soft, round white idlis on a banana leaf with a cup of sambar and a spoonful of white coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Raw rice works but gives slightly firmer idlis; a handful of poha ground with the rice softens them.
Replace up to half the idli rice with foxtail millet soaked the same way; the idlis will be a little denser.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge and turns more sour. Cooked idlis keep 1 day refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes, or microwave covered with a damp cloth for 30 to 40 seconds.

recipes.title: Crisp Plain Dosa
recipes.description: Golden, paper-thin dosas from a thinner, rice-heavy batter of raw and parboiled rice with a little urad dal and chana dal for colour. Makes about 16 dosas; one serving = 2 dosas.

steps.title: Soak the grains
steps.text: Wash both rices together and soak them in one bowl. Wash the urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek together and soak them in another. Soak both for 5 hours.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls: one of white raw rice and opaque parboiled rice under water, the other of white urad dal, yellow chana dal and fenugreek seeds

steps.title: Grind the dals
steps.text: Drain the dals and grind with a little cold water for 5 to 6 minutes to a smooth, fluffy paste. Transfer to a large bowl.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale cream dal paste in a mixer jar, a spatula scraping down the sides

steps.title: Grind the rice smooth
steps.text: Grind the drained rice with water until completely smooth, finer than idli batter, with no grit when rubbed between your fingers. Add it to the dal paste.
steps.visual: Silky, smooth rice batter flowing from the mixer jar into the large steel mixing bowl of dal paste

steps.title: Salt and ferment
steps.text: Stir in the salt, mixing well by hand. Cover and ferment for 6 to 8 hours until bubbly and slightly risen. Dosa batter rises less than idli batter, and that is fine.
steps.visual: The large steel bowl of creamy batter with a bubbly, slightly risen surface after fermenting

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Stir the batter and add water a few spoons at a time until it flows like thick buttermilk and coats the back of a ladle thinly. Thinner batter gives crisper dosas.
steps.visual: A steel ladle lifted out of the thinned batter, a smooth, thin coating dripping off it back into the bowl

steps.title: Season the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron tawa on medium-high heat. Rub a few drops of oil over it with a folded cloth, then sprinkle a little water; it should sizzle off at once. Lower the heat to medium.
steps.visual: Water droplets sizzling and evaporating on a lightly oiled black cast-iron tawa

steps.title: Spread thin
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and, using the back of the ladle, quickly spread it in outward spirals into a thin 9-inch crepe.
steps.visual: A thin, lacy circle of white batter being spread in spirals with the back of a ladle across the black tawa

steps.title: Crisp the dosa
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and over the top. Cook for 1½ to 2 minutes without flipping until the underside is golden and the edges lift away from the tawa.
steps.visual: A thin dosa on the tawa turning golden-brown, the edges curling up and tiny oil bubbles on top

steps.title: Fold and serve
steps.text: Fold or roll the dosa and serve straight away with sambar and chutney. Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas and repeat with the remaining batter.
steps.visual: A crisp, golden rolled plain dosa on a steel plate with a cup of sambar and a spoonful of coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Ghee gives a richer, nuttier crust; use the same amount.
Leave out the chana dal if you don't have it; the dosas will be paler but still crisp.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 3 days refrigerated; bring it to room temperature before cooking.
recipes.reheating: Dosas are best cooked fresh; warm leftovers briefly on a hot tawa.

recipes.title: Instant Oats Idli
recipes.description: No-ferment idlis of toasted, powdered oats with a little rava and curd, studded with carrot and a mustard–curry leaf tempering. Ready in about 40 minutes. Makes 16 idlis; one serving = 4 idlis.

steps.title: Toast and powder the oats
steps.text: Dry roast the oats in a kadai on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Cool for a few minutes, then grind to a fine powder in the mixer.
steps.visual: Lightly toasted oats in a black kadai, and beside it a mixer jar holding fine, pale oat powder

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadai on medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the urad dal, chana dal and cashews (if using) and fry until golden, then add the curry leaves, green chilli and ginger for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Golden urad and chana dal, cashew pieces, crackling curry leaves and chopped green chilli in shimmering oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Roast the rava
steps.text: Add the rava to the tempering and roast on low heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty. Turn off the heat.
steps.visual: Pale rava coated in the tempering in the black kadai, dotted with mustard seeds and curry leaves

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Tip the rava mixture into a bowl with the oat powder, grated carrot, coriander and salt. Add the curd and water and mix to a thick, scoopable batter like idli batter.
steps.visual: Thick, speckled oat batter with orange carrot shreds and green coriander in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15 minutes so the oats and rava absorb the liquid. If it gets too stiff, stir in 1 to 2 tbsp water.
steps.visual: The same bowl of batter, now thicker and set, with a spoon standing upright in it

steps.title: Add soda and aerate
steps.text: Bring water to a boil in the steamer and grease the idli plates. Just before steaming, sprinkle the baking soda over the batter, pour 1 tsp water on it and fold gently until the batter turns light and airy.
steps.visual: Light, airy batter being folded in the steel bowl beside greased idli plates

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds and steam on medium heat for 12 minutes (no whistle on a pressure cooker) until a toothpick comes out clean.
steps.visual: An idli stand of filled moulds inside a steaming pot with the lid lifted, the oat idlis risen and set

steps.title: Unmould and serve
steps.text: Rest the idlis for 3 minutes, unmould with a wet spoon and serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.
steps.visual: Four golden-flecked oat idlis with visible carrot and coriander on a steel plate beside green coconut chutney and a cup of sambar

substitutions.note: Ragi flour in place of rava gives darker, earthier idlis; oats themselves may contain gluten unless labelled gluten-free.
If your curd is very sour, use half curd and half water so the idlis aren't too tangy.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; cooked idlis keep 1 day refrigerated. Don't store the batter once soda is added.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes or microwave covered for 40 seconds.

recipes.title: Jeera Rice
recipes.description: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with cumin seeds toasted in ghee and a few whole spices, a simple base for dal, rajma and paneer curries. One serving = about 1 cup cooked (60 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse and soak
steps.text: Rinse the basmati gently 3 times until the water runs clear, then soak it in fresh water for 20 minutes. Drain well.
steps.visual: Long, slender basmati grains soaking in clear water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Toast the cumin
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy saucepan on medium heat. Add the bay leaves, cloves and cardamom, then the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds until they darken a shade.
steps.visual: Cumin seeds sizzling and browning in golden ghee with bay leaves, cloves and cardamom pods in a heavy steel saucepan

steps.title: Coat the rice
steps.text: Add the drained rice and stir gently for 1 to 2 minutes so every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.visual: Basmati grains glossy with ghee and flecked with cumin seeds in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the salt and bring to a boil.
steps.visual: Rice and whole spices under bubbling water in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the water is absorbed. In a pressure cooker, use 1½ cups water and cook for 1 whistle. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.
steps.visual: The saucepan lid lifted to show cooked rice with small steam holes on its surface and cumin seeds on top

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, scatter over the coriander if using, and serve with dal tadka, rajma or a paneer curry.
steps.visual: Long, separate grains of jeera rice flecked with cumin and coriander in a white bowl, a bowl of yellow dal beside it

substitutions.note: Brown rice needs a 30-minute soak, 2½ cups water and 20 to 25 minutes of covered cooking.
Use oil to make it vegan.

recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered, or warm in a covered pan on low heat.

recipes.title: Light Vegetable Quinoa Pulao
recipes.description: Quinoa cooked pulao-style with whole spices, mint, carrot, beans and peas in one pan. A light base for dal, kadhi or a chicken curry. One serving = about 1¼ cups.

steps.title: Rinse the quinoa
steps.text: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under running water for about a minute, rubbing it with your fingers to wash off its bitter coating. Drain well.
steps.visual: Small ivory quinoa seeds in a fine steel sieve under running water

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Slice the onion, slit the chilli, grate the ginger, dice the carrot, chop the beans and pick the mint leaves.
steps.visual: Sliced onion, diced carrot, chopped beans, green peas, a slit green chilli, grated ginger and mint leaves in separate piles on a wooden board

steps.title: Sizzle the whole spices
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy saucepan on medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
steps.visual: Cumin seeds, a bay leaf, cloves and a cinnamon stick sizzling in ghee in a heavy steel saucepan

steps.title: Sauté onion and vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, green chilli and ginger and cook for 3 minutes until the onion softens. Add the carrot, beans and peas and sauté for 2 minutes more.
steps.visual: Softened onion with carrot cubes, beans and peas glistening among the whole spices in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Add quinoa and water
steps.text: Add the drained quinoa and stir with the vegetables for 1 minute. Pour in the water, add the salt and half the mint, and bring to a boil.
steps.visual: Quinoa and vegetables under bubbling water in the saucepan, a few mint leaves floating on top

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat for 13 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and each grain shows a little white tail. In a pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
steps.visual: The lid lifted to show fluffy quinoa with visible curly white germ rings, studded with carrot and peas

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, fold in the remaining mint and the lemon juice if using, and serve with dal, kadhi or a curry.
steps.visual: Fluffy vegetable quinoa pulao in a ceramic bowl with carrot, beans, peas and fresh mint on top

substitutions.note: Foxtail millet works with about 2¼ cups water per cup and 15 minutes of covered cooking.
Use oil to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; it packs well for lunch boxes.
recipes.reheating: Microwave covered with a splash of water for 1 to 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Beetroot Poriyal
recipes.description: Sweet, earthy diced beetroot cooked with shallots, green chilli and ginger in coconut oil and finished with fresh coconut — a colourful side for any rice meal.

steps.title: Dice the beetroot
steps.text: Peel the beetroot and cut it into small, even 5 mm dice. Smaller pieces cook faster and stay juicy.
steps.visual: A heap of tiny, deep magenta beetroot cubes on a wooden board stained pink, peelings at the side

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add urad dal and curry leaves and fry until the dal is golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden urad dal and curry leaves in coconut oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté the aromatics
steps.text: Add the shallots, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 2 minutes until the shallots soften.
steps.visual: Softened pink shallots, chopped green chilli and ginger sizzling with the tempering in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the beetroot
steps.text: Add the beetroot, salt and water. Cover and cook on low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beetroot is tender and the water has evaporated.
steps.visual: Glossy magenta beetroot cubes in the covered black iron kadai, a little pink steam rising as the lid lifts

steps.title: Add coconut
steps.text: Stir in the grated coconut and cook for 1 minute more.
steps.visual: White grated coconut turning pink as it is tossed through the beetroot in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and sambar, rasam or curd rice.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of bright magenta beetroot poriyal flecked with coconut and curry leaves beside a plate of curd rice

substitutions.note: Chopped onion works just as well.
Carrot poriyal is made exactly the same way.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan for 1 to 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Vendakkai (Okra) Poriyal
recipes.description: Crisp-edged okra rounds stir-fried with onion, chilli powder and turmeric until no longer slimy. Simple, spicy and great with sambar rice or curd rice.

ingredients.prep: washed, dried, cut in ½-inch rounds

steps.title: Wash and dry the okra
steps.text: Wash the okra and spread it on a kitchen towel until completely dry — wet okra turns slimy. Trim the ends and cut into ½-inch rounds.
steps.visual: Green okra rounds with pale seeds showing, spread on a wooden board, trimmed tops pushed to one side and a cotton towel behind

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide kadai over medium heat. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add urad dal and curry leaves.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds popping with urad dal and curry leaves in oil in a wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and sauté for 2 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Soft translucent onion among the tempering in the wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Fry the okra uncovered
steps.text: Add the okra and turmeric. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring gently every couple of minutes. Don't cover and don't add salt yet — both make okra sticky.
steps.visual: Green okra rounds spread out in the wide black iron kadai, edges starting to brown, no stickiness visible

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: When the okra is tender and the edges are crisp, add the salt, chilli powder and coriander powder. Toss for 2 minutes on low heat until coated.
steps.visual: Crisp okra rounds coated in red chilli and coriander powder in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with sambar rice, rasam rice or curd rice.
steps.visual: Spicy, crisp okra poriyal heaped in a steel bowl, red-tinged and flecked with curry leaves, beside curd rice

substitutions.note: Sambar powder in place of chilli and coriander powders gives a more rounded flavour.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in a hot pan without a lid.

recipes.title: Chow Chow Milagu Kootu
recipes.description: Tender chayote and chana dal simmered in a pepper, cumin and coconut paste — a mild, creamy Tamil kootu that pairs well with rasam and a spicy fry.

steps.title: Soak the chana dal
steps.text: Wash the chana dal and soak it in water for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Yellow chana dal soaking in water in a small steel bowl

steps.title: Pressure-cook the dal
steps.text: Drain and pressure-cook the dal with 1 cup of water for 3 whistles, about 10 minutes, until soft but still holding its shape.
steps.visual: Soft, whole yellow chana dal grains in a little cooking water in the open pressure cooker

steps.title: Cook the chow chow
steps.text: Put the chow chow cubes in a saucepan with 1 cup of water, the turmeric and salt. Simmer covered for 8 minutes until just tender.
steps.visual: Pale green chow chow cubes simmering in yellow-tinged water in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Grind the pepper paste
steps.text: Grind the coconut, black pepper, cumin and red chillies with ¼ cup of water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: Smooth, creamy white coconut paste speckled with black pepper in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer the kootu
steps.text: Add the cooked dal and the coconut paste to the chow chow. Simmer on low for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy. Add a little water if it's too thick.
steps.visual: Creamy, pale yellow kootu with chow chow cubes and whole chana dal gently bubbling in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small kadai, pop the mustard seeds, then fry the urad dal until golden and add curry leaves. Pour over the kootu.
steps.visual: Golden tempering of mustard seeds, urad dal and curry leaves being poured from a small black kadai onto the kootu

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and rasam, or with chapati.
steps.visual: Chow chow kootu in a steel bowl topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves, beside a bowl of rasam and rice

substitutions.note: Bottle gourd or snake gourd make an equally good kootu.
Moong dal cooks faster and needs no soaking.

recipes.reheating: Warm with a splash of water, stirring.

recipes.title: Cabbage Moong Dal Kootu
recipes.description: Soft moong dal and shredded cabbage simmered with a coconut, green chilli and cumin paste, finished with a red chilli and hing tempering.

steps.title: Cook the moong dal
steps.text: Wash the moong dal and simmer it with 1½ cups of water and the turmeric in a saucepan for 15 minutes until soft and just starting to break down.
steps.visual: Soft, pale-yellow moong dal simmering in a steel saucepan, a little foam at the edges

steps.title: Add the cabbage
steps.text: Add the shredded cabbage, salt and ½ cup of water. Cover and cook for 6 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
steps.visual: Shredded pale green cabbage wilting into the yellow dal in the covered steel saucepan

steps.title: Grind the coconut paste
steps.text: Grind the coconut, green chilli and cumin with 3 tablespoons of water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale green-white coconut and chilli paste in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer with the paste
steps.text: Stir the paste into the dal and cabbage and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and creamy.
steps.visual: Thick, creamy cabbage and dal kootu gently bubbling in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a small kadai. Pop the mustard seeds, then add urad dal, red chilli, hing and curry leaves. When the dal turns golden, pour the tempering over the kootu.
steps.visual: Sizzling mustard seeds, golden urad dal, a red chilli and curry leaves in a small black kadai held over the kootu

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with rice and rasam or with chapati.
steps.visual: A steel bowl of creamy cabbage kootu topped with the red chilli and curry leaf tempering

substitutions.note: Spinach makes a quick keerai kootu — cook it for only 3 minutes.
Use gluten-free hing if needed.

recipes.reheating: Warm with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Vendakkai Mor Kuzhambu
recipes.description: Tangy curd gravy thickened with a ground coconut, ginger, green chilli and soaked dal paste, with pan-fried okra. Warming, mild and gently sour.

steps.title: Soak dal and coriander
steps.text: Soak the toor dal and coriander seeds together in warm water for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Toor dal and coriander seeds soaking in a small steel bowl of water

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Drain and grind the dal and coriander with the coconut, green chillies, ginger and cumin, adding a little water, to a very smooth paste.
steps.visual: Very smooth, creamy pale-green coconut paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Whisk the curd base
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the water, ground paste, turmeric and salt in a bowl until completely smooth.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale yellow curd and coconut mixture in a steel mixing bowl with a whisk

steps.title: Fry the okra
steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons of the coconut oil in a kadai and fry the okra pieces uncovered on medium heat for 7 to 8 minutes until tender and lightly browned. Push them to one side.
steps.visual: Lightly browned green okra pieces in coconut oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Temper in the same kadai
steps.text: Add the remaining oil, then mustard seeds, fenugreek, red chillies, hing and curry leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, red chillies and curry leaves crackling beside the browned okra in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Heat the curd gently
steps.text: Turn the heat to low and pour in the curd mixture. Stir continuously for 4 to 5 minutes until it is hot and frothy at the edges. Do not let it boil or the curd will split.
steps.visual: Pale yellow mor kuzhambu turning frothy at the edges in the black iron kadai, okra pieces and red chillies floating in it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat as soon as it froths. Serve warm with rice and a dry poriyal or paruppu usili.
steps.visual: Vendakkai mor kuzhambu in a steel bowl, creamy yellow with okra, curry leaves and red chillies, rice and beans poriyal alongside

substitutions.note: Boiled ash gourd or chow chow are traditional alternatives.
Thinned hung curd gives a thicker, higher-protein gravy.

recipes.reheating: Warm on very low heat, stirring, without boiling.

recipes.title: Ennai Kathirikai Kuzhambu
recipes.description: Whole baby brinjals braised in gingelly oil in a thick tamarind gravy with a roasted coriander, chilli, sesame and coconut masala. Tangy, rich and better the next day.

steps.title: Roast the masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the coriander seeds, chana dal and red chillies in a kadai on low heat for 3 minutes until the dal is golden. Add the sesame seeds and coconut and roast 1 minute more until the coconut is light brown.
steps.visual: Golden chana dal, coriander seeds, dark red chillies, sesame seeds and light-brown coconut roasting in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind and soak
steps.text: Cool the roasted masala and grind it with ½ cup of water to a smooth paste. Soak the tamarind in 1 cup of warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice.
steps.visual: A mixer jar of thick reddish-brown masala paste beside a steel bowl of dark tamarind water

steps.title: Fry the brinjals
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in the same kadai over medium heat. Fry the slit brinjals for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until the skins wrinkle and the flesh softens. Lift them out.
steps.visual: Small purple brinjals with wrinkled, glossy skins frying in gingelly oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Temper and sauté
steps.text: In the same oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add fenugreek and curry leaves. Add the shallots and garlic and sauté for 4 minutes until golden, then the tomato, turmeric and chilli powder until the tomato is mushy.
steps.visual: Golden whole shallots and garlic cloves with softened tomato and curry leaves in red-tinged oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind water, the masala paste and the remaining water. Add salt and jaggery and bring to a boil, then return the brinjals to the kadai.
steps.visual: Reddish-brown tamarind gravy bubbling in the black iron kadai with the fried brinjals being returned to it

steps.title: Cook until oil separates
steps.text: Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the gravy thickens and the gingelly oil floats to the top.
steps.visual: Thick, dark red kuzhambu with a sheen of oil floating on top, whole brinjals and shallots nestled in it, in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with rice and a spoon of ghee, or with idli and dosa.
steps.visual: Ennai kathirikai kuzhambu in a clay pot, glossy oil-topped gravy with whole brinjals, rice and appalam beside it on a banana leaf

substitutions.note: Leave out the jaggery to cut sugar — the gravy will be sharper.
Chopped onion can stand in for shallots.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the flavour improves overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently until just simmering.

recipes.title: Sundakkai Vatha Kuzhambu
recipes.description: A thick, tangy tamarind gravy with fried dried turkey berries, garlic and shallots in plenty of gingelly oil. A little goes a long way with hot rice.

steps.title: Extract the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1½ cups of warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze well and strain the juice, discarding the fibres.
steps.visual: Thick, dark brown tamarind juice in a steel bowl with squeezed tamarind pulp in a strainer above it

steps.title: Fry the sundakkai
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in a heavy kadai on low-medium heat. Fry the sundakkai vathal for 1 minute until it turns dark and crisp — watch closely, it burns fast. Lift out and keep aside.
steps.visual: Small, shrivelled, dark brown dried turkey berries sizzling in gingelly oil in a heavy black kadai

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: In the same oil add the mustard seeds; when they pop add fenugreek, toor dal, red chillies, hing and curry leaves and fry until the dal turns golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden toor dal and fenugreek, red chillies and curry leaves in oil in the heavy black kadai

steps.title: Sauté garlic and shallots
steps.text: Add the whole garlic cloves and shallots and sauté for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and soft.
steps.visual: Whole golden garlic cloves and glossy shallots in the tempering in the heavy black kadai

steps.title: Add the spice powders
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the sambar powder and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds without letting them burn.
steps.visual: Garlic and shallots coated in deep red sambar powder in the heavy black kadai

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind juice and the remaining water, add salt, jaggery and the fried sundakkai. Simmer on low for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy is thick and oil floats on top.
steps.visual: Thick, glossy, almost black-brown kuzhambu with oil pooling on the surface, garlic, shallots and dark sundakkai visible, in the heavy black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve a small ladleful over hot rice with a little ghee or gingelly oil, alongside a poriyal and appalam.
steps.visual: A small stone bowl of dark, glossy vatha kuzhambu with garlic and sundakkai, beside rice, ghee and a beans poriyal on a banana leaf

substitutions.note: Manathakkali vathal is a common alternative; or skip it for a plain poondu (garlic) kuzhambu.
Leave out the jaggery to cut sugar.

recipes.storage: Keeps up to 5 days refrigerated thanks to the tamarind and oil.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat.

recipes.title: Milagu Rasam
recipes.description: A sharp, warming pepper rasam made with a freshly roasted pepper, cumin and coriander powder, tamarind and crushed garlic, tempered in ghee. Sip it hot or mix with rice.

steps.title: Roast and grind the spices
steps.text: Dry-roast the pepper, cumin, coriander seeds, toor dal and red chillies in a kadai on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and the dal turns golden. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
steps.visual: Black peppercorns, cumin, coriander seeds, golden toor dal and red chillies roasting in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Make tamarind water
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup of warm water for 10 minutes, squeeze and strain.
steps.visual: Light brown tamarind water in a steel bowl, squeezed pulp at the side

steps.title: Boil the tamarind base
steps.text: In a saucepan, boil the tamarind water with the crushed garlic, turmeric and salt for 5 minutes until the raw tamarind smell goes.
steps.visual: Tamarind water with crushed garlic boiling in a steel rasam saucepan

steps.title: Add the pepper powder
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the ground pepper powder. Heat on low until it froths up, about 3 minutes, then turn off the heat — don't let rasam boil hard after this.
steps.visual: Thin, peppery brown rasam frothing at the top in the steel saucepan, flecks of ground spice floating

steps.title: Temper in ghee
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a small kadai, pop the mustard seeds, add curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam. Add the coriander and cover for 2 minutes.
steps.visual: Ghee tempering with mustard seeds and curry leaves sizzling on top of the rasam, chopped coriander floating

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot in small cups to sip, or pour over rice with a poriyal on the side.
steps.visual: Two steel tumblers of steaming, peppery milagu rasam with curry leaves and coriander on top

substitutions.note: Temper in gingelly oil for a vegan rasam.
Use gluten-free hing if needed.

recipes.reheating: Warm until it just froths; boiling makes rasam bitter.

recipes.title: Tomato Rasam
recipes.description: Bright, tangy rasam of ripe tomatoes and a little tamarind, flavoured with freshly crushed pepper, cumin and garlic — no rasam powder needed.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic together in a mortar and pestle.
steps.visual: Coarsely crushed black pepper, cumin and garlic in a stone mortar with the pestle resting in it

steps.title: Mash the tomatoes
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup of warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice. Squeeze the chopped tomatoes by hand into the tamarind water until pulpy.
steps.visual: Squeezed red tomato pulp and skins in brown tamarind water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: Pour the tomato–tamarind mixture into a saucepan with 1 cup of water, the crushed spices, turmeric and salt. Boil for 8 minutes until the tomatoes are completely soft.
steps.visual: Red tomato and tamarind broth boiling in a steel saucepan with crushed pepper and garlic visible

steps.title: Dilute and froth
steps.text: Add the remaining water and heat on low until the rasam froths up at the top, about 3 minutes. Turn off the heat.
steps.visual: Thin orange-red rasam with a frothy surface in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a small kadai, pop the mustard seeds, then add red chillies, curry leaves and hing. Pour over the rasam and add the coriander.
steps.visual: Sizzling mustard seeds, a red chilli and curry leaves landing on the orange rasam, chopped coriander floating on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with rice and a poriyal, or as a light soup.
steps.visual: A steel bowl of clear orange-red tomato rasam with coriander and curry leaves on top, rice and poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: If your tomatoes are very sour, skip the tamarind and finish with a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.reheating: Warm until it just froths.

recipes.title: Paruppu Rasam
recipes.description: Comforting dal rasam: cooked toor dal and tomato in a light tamarind broth with rasam powder, finished with ghee, cumin and fresh coriander.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Wash the toor dal and pressure-cook it with 1 cup of the water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, about 15 minutes. Mash it smooth and thin it with 1 cup of water.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale yellow mashed dal being thinned with water in the open pressure cooker

steps.title: Boil tamarind and tomato
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup of warm water and extract the juice. Boil it in a saucepan with the tomato, rasam powder and salt for 8 minutes until the tomato is soft and the raw smell is gone.
steps.visual: Tomato pieces in reddish tamarind water boiling with rasam powder in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Add the dal water
steps.text: Pour in the thinned dal and the remaining water and heat on low until the rasam rises and froths, about 3 minutes. Turn off the heat before it boils.
steps.visual: Cloudy golden rasam frothing at the top of the steel saucepan, tomato pieces floating

steps.title: Temper in ghee
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a small kadai, pop the mustard seeds, add cumin, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam. Stir in the coriander.
steps.visual: Ghee tempering with mustard, cumin and curry leaves sizzling as it hits the golden rasam, coriander scattered on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot over rice with a poriyal, or in a cup as a soup.
steps.visual: Golden paruppu rasam in a steel bowl with coriander and curry leaves, a mound of rice and beetroot poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Use gingelly oil to make it vegan.
Moong dal makes a lighter rasam and needs only 2 whistles.

recipes.reheating: Warm until it just froths; don't boil.

recipes.title: Chettinad Egg Curry
recipes.description: Boiled eggs simmered in a Chettinad gravy of onion and tomato with a freshly roasted coconut, red chilli, coriander and pepper masala, tempered with fennel and whole spices.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Cover the eggs with water in a saucepan, bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel and make 3 or 4 shallow slits on each egg so the gravy soaks in.
steps.visual: Six peeled, white hard-boiled eggs with shallow slits in a steel bowl, shells on a plate beside

steps.title: Roast the masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the coriander seeds, red chillies, pepper and cumin in a kadai on low heat for 2 minutes. Add the coconut and roast until it turns light golden, about 2 minutes more.
steps.visual: Coriander seeds, red chillies, peppercorns, cumin and golden coconut roasting together in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Cool the roasted masala and grind it with ½ cup of water to a smooth paste.
steps.visual: Thick, smooth brick-red masala paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Temper and brown the onion
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in the same kadai. Add cinnamon, cloves, fennel and curry leaves, then the onion. Sauté on medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until golden brown.
steps.visual: Golden brown onions with fennel seeds, a cinnamon stick and curry leaves in oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the tomato base
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute. Add tomato, turmeric and chilli powder and cook until the tomato is mushy and oil starts to separate, about 4 minutes.
steps.visual: Thick red onion–tomato masala with oil glistening at the edges of the black iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Stir in the ground masala, the water and salt. Simmer on low for 8 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns deep red-brown.
steps.visual: Deep red-brown Chettinad gravy simmering in the black iron kadai, small bubbles breaking on the surface

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Slide in the slit eggs, spoon the gravy over them and simmer for 5 minutes so they absorb the flavour.
steps.visual: Whole slit boiled eggs half-submerged in thick red-brown gravy in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter coriander and serve with rice, dosa or chapati, plus a vegetable poriyal.
steps.visual: Chettinad egg curry in a brass bowl, halved eggs showing yellow yolks in thick red gravy topped with coriander, a dosa beside it

substitutions.note: Ground cashews give a creamier, coconut-free gravy.
Shallots give a sweeter, more traditional Chettinad flavour.

recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat, adding a splash of water.

recipes.title: Chettinad Mushroom Masala
recipes.description: Button mushrooms cooked in a thick, spicy Chettinad masala of shallots, tomato and a roasted fennel, pepper, coriander and coconut paste with star anise and cardamom.

steps.title: Roast the Chettinad masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the red chillies, coriander seeds, fennel and pepper in a kadai on low heat for 2 minutes until aromatic. Add the coconut and roast for another 2 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Red chillies, coriander seeds, fennel, black pepper and golden coconut roasting in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind and clean
steps.text: Cool and grind the roasted masala with ¼ cup water to a thick paste. Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth and cut them into halves or quarters.
steps.visual: A mixer jar of thick red-brown masala paste beside halved white button mushrooms on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadai. Add star anise, cardamom and curry leaves, then the shallots, and sauté for 5 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced shallots with a star anise, cardamom pods and curry leaves in oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and tomato
steps.text: Add the crushed ginger and garlic and sauté for a minute, then add the tomato and turmeric and cook until the tomato breaks down, about 3 minutes.
steps.visual: Soft, broken-down tomato with shallots, crushed ginger and garlic in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the masala paste
steps.text: Stir in the ground masala and cook on low heat for 2 minutes until the oil starts to separate.
steps.visual: Thick, dark red Chettinad masala with oil glistening at the edges of the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the mushrooms
steps.text: Add the mushrooms and salt and toss on high heat for 2 minutes. They will release water. Add the water and cook uncovered on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the masala clings thickly to the mushrooms.
steps.visual: Mushroom pieces coated in a thick, glossy red-brown masala in the black iron kadai, most liquid cooked away

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot with chapati, dosa or rice.
steps.visual: Chettinad mushroom masala in a brass kadai-style serving bowl topped with coriander and curry leaves, a stack of dosas beside it

substitutions.note: Paneer cubes make a higher-protein version; add them in the last 3 minutes.
Use sliced onion if shallots aren't available.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan over medium heat.

recipes.title: Kozhi Milagu Rasam (Chicken Pepper Soup)
recipes.description: A peppery, thin Tamil chicken soup cooked with bone-in chicken, shallots, garlic and a freshly ground pepper, cumin and coriander mix. Traditionally made with nattu kozhi (country chicken).

steps.title: Grind the pepper mix
steps.text: Coarsely grind the pepper, cumin, coriander seeds, fennel and red chillies in a dry mixer jar or crush them in a mortar.
steps.visual: Coarse brown spice powder with cracked peppercorns and coriander husks in a small mixer jar

steps.title: Crush the aromatics
steps.text: Wash the chicken and drain. Lightly crush the shallots, garlic and ginger together so they release their juices.
steps.visual: Small bone-in chicken pieces in a steel bowl beside lightly crushed shallots, garlic and ginger on a wooden board

steps.title: Sauté in the cooker
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in the pressure cooker base. Add curry leaves and the crushed aromatics and sauté for 3 minutes. Add tomato and turmeric and cook until soft.
steps.visual: Crushed shallots, garlic, ginger, curry leaves and softened tomato sizzling in oil in the base of a steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and the ground pepper mix and stir on medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the chicken turns opaque and the spices smell toasted.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces coated in coarse brown pepper masala in the pressure cooker base, edges turning white and lightly browned

steps.title: Pressure-cook the soup
steps.text: Pour in the water and add salt. Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 4 whistles, about 18 minutes (country chicken needs 7 to 8 whistles). Let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.visual: The closed steel pressure cooker on the stove with steam escaping from the whistle

steps.title: Simmer and season
steps.text: Open the cooker, check the salt and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes. The rasam should be thin and peppery. Stir in the coriander.
steps.visual: Thin, golden-brown peppery broth with chicken pieces and curry leaves simmering in the open pressure cooker, coriander floating on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve piping hot in bowls with the chicken pieces, as a soup or poured over rice.
steps.visual: A deep bowl of steaming peppery chicken rasam with bone-in chicken pieces, curry leaves and coriander, a lime wedge beside

substitutions.note: Mutton bones make a classic aattu kaal-style soup; cook for 8 whistles.
A spoon of ghee gives a richer finish.

recipes.reheating: Bring back to a simmer before serving.

recipes.title: Mutton Chukka
recipes.description: Madurai-style dry mutton roast: tender bone-in mutton cooked down with shallots and curry leaves, then roasted dark with a freshly ground pepper, chilli and fennel masala.

steps.title: Pressure-cook the mutton
steps.text: Wash the mutton and pressure-cook it with the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, salt and water for 6 whistles, about 25 minutes, until tender. Keep the stock.
steps.visual: Tender bone-in mutton pieces in a little yellow stock in an open steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Roast and grind the masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the red chillies, coriander seeds, pepper, cumin and half the fennel in a kadai on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
steps.visual: Red chillies, coriander seeds, peppercorns, cumin and fennel toasting in a dry black iron kadai

steps.title: Temper and fry shallots
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in the same kadai. Add the remaining fennel, cinnamon, cloves and curry leaves, then the shallots, and sauté for 6 minutes until deep golden.
steps.visual: Deep golden sliced shallots with fennel seeds, cinnamon, cloves and crisp curry leaves in oil in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Reduce with the stock
steps.text: Add the cooked mutton with its stock and cook on medium-high heat, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until the stock has almost completely reduced.
steps.visual: Mutton pieces in a reducing brown stock with shallots in the black iron kadai, liquid bubbling away

steps.title: Roast with the masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in the ground masala and roast on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the mutton is dark, dry and coated.
steps.visual: Dark, dry-roasted mutton chunks coated in coarse red-brown pepper masala and curry leaves in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot with rasam rice or a light dal and a vegetable poriyal.
steps.visual: Dark mutton chukka heaped on a banana leaf garnished with coriander and fried curry leaves, a bowl of rasam beside it

substitutions.note: For chicken chukka, skip the pressure cooker and cook covered for 15 minutes before roasting.
Thinly sliced onion works if shallots aren't available.

recipes.reheating: Reheat in a hot pan with a teaspoon of water.

recipes.title: Tamil Meen Kuzhambu (Mackerel)
recipes.description: Madurai-style tangy fish curry: mackerel simmered in a thick tamarind, shallot and tomato gravy with chilli and coriander powders, tempered with fenugreek in gingelly oil.

steps.title: Clean the fish
steps.text: Wash the mackerel pieces in water with a pinch of turmeric and salt, rinse and drain.
steps.visual: Cleaned, thick mackerel pieces with silvery-blue skin on a steel plate

steps.title: Prepare the tamarind gravy
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in 1 cup of warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice. Mix in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and the remaining water.
steps.visual: Thin, brick-red spiced tamarind liquid in a steel bowl, squeezed tamarind pulp beside it

steps.title: Temper in gingelly oil
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in a kadai or clay pot over medium heat. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add fenugreek and curry leaves.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden fenugreek and crackling curry leaves in gingelly oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Sauté shallots, garlic and tomato
steps.text: Add the shallots and garlic and sauté for 4 minutes until golden. Add the tomato and cook until it is completely mushy, about 4 minutes.
steps.visual: Golden shallots and garlic with collapsed tomato in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Pour in the spiced tamarind liquid and add salt. Simmer on medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the raw smell of the spices is gone and the gravy thickens with oil rising to the top.
steps.visual: Thick, deep red tamarind gravy simmering in the black kadai with a film of oil on top

steps.title: Cook the fish
steps.text: Slide the fish pieces into the gravy in one layer. Don't stir — swirl the pot gently. Simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish is just cooked through.
steps.visual: Mackerel pieces submerged in thick red gravy in the black kadai, oil pooling on the surface, curry leaves scattered

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat and rest for at least 30 minutes — meen kuzhambu tastes best a few hours after cooking. Serve with rice and a poriyal, or with dosa.
steps.visual: Tamil meen kuzhambu in a clay pot, glossy red gravy with mackerel pieces and shallots, rice and cabbage poriyal on a banana leaf beside

substitutions.note: Seer fish (vanjaram) holds its shape well; sardines are a cheaper option.
Skip the tomato for a sharper, more tamarind-forward kuzhambu.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; the flavour improves overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently without stirring until just bubbling.

recipes.title: Eral Thokku (Prawn Thokku)
recipes.description: Prawns cooked in a thick, spicy Tamil masala of slow-browned onions, tomato, chilli and coriander powders, finished with crushed black pepper.

steps.title: Marinate the prawns
steps.text: Rinse and drain the prawns, then toss them with the turmeric and a pinch of salt. Set aside for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Cleaned, deveined pink-grey prawns tinged yellow with turmeric in a steel bowl

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Heat the gingelly oil in a kadai. Add fennel seeds and curry leaves, then the onion and green chilli. Sauté on medium heat for 8 minutes until the onions are deep golden.
steps.visual: Deep golden chopped onions with slit green chillies, fennel and curry leaves in oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the tomato masala
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute. Add the tomato, chilli powder, coriander powder and the remaining salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, mashing, until thick and the oil separates.
steps.visual: Thick, jammy dark red onion–tomato masala with oil separating at the edges of the black iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Add the prawns and stir to coat. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until they curl and turn pink and the masala clings to them. Don't overcook or they will toughen.
steps.visual: Curled pink prawns coated in a thick red masala in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Finish with pepper
steps.text: Sprinkle the crushed pepper and toss for 1 minute on high heat until the thokku is thick and dry.
steps.visual: Glossy prawn thokku flecked with black pepper in the black iron kadai, no liquid left

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with rice and rasam, dosa or chapati.
steps.visual: Prawn thokku in a steel bowl garnished with coriander and curry leaves, a dosa and rasam beside it

substitutions.note: Squid rings make a good thokku; cook them for only 3 to 4 minutes.
Shallots give a sweeter masala.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Vanjaram Tawa Fish Fry
recipes.description: Chennai-style seer fish steaks rubbed with a spicy chilli, pepper, ginger-garlic and lemon masala and shallow-fried on a cast-iron tawa until crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Clean the fish
steps.text: Wash the fish steaks and pat them completely dry with a kitchen towel — dry fish crisps better.
steps.visual: Four clean, pale seer-fish steaks laid on a kitchen towel on a steel tray

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: In a bowl mix the chilli powder, Kashmiri chilli, turmeric, crushed pepper, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste. Add a teaspoon of water only if needed.
steps.visual: A thick, deep red masala paste in a small steel bowl with a spoon

steps.title: Coat and marinate
steps.text: Rub the masala all over both sides of the fish steaks. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Seer-fish steaks thickly coated in red masala on the steel tray, covered with a plate

steps.title: Fry the first side
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron tawa on medium heat and spread half the oil. Place the steaks on the tawa with the curry leaves around them and fry for 4 to 5 minutes without moving them, until a crisp crust forms.
steps.visual: Red masala-coated fish steaks sizzling on a black cast-iron tawa with curry leaves frying around them

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Drizzle the remaining oil around the fish, flip carefully with a flat spatula and fry the other side for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
steps.visual: Flipped fish steaks with a dark red, crisp, slightly charred crust on the black tawa, fried curry leaves on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with the fried curry leaves, onion rings and a lemon wedge, alongside rasam rice or a salad.
steps.visual: Crisp red vanjaram fish steaks on a banana leaf with fried curry leaves, sliced onion rings and a lemon wedge

substitutions.note: Whole pomfret or mackerel can be fried the same way; score the flesh so the masala penetrates.
Coconut oil gives a coastal flavour.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp on a hot tawa or in an air fryer at 180°C for 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Muttai Podimas (Egg Podimas)
recipes.description: Tamil-style scrambled egg cooked with onion, green chilli, curry leaves and a crunchy urad dal tempering, finished with crushed pepper and coriander.

steps.title: Beat the eggs
steps.text: Beat the eggs with the salt in a bowl until frothy.
steps.visual: Frothy beaten eggs in a steel bowl with a fork

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai over medium heat. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add urad dal and fry until golden, then add curry leaves.
steps.visual: Golden urad dal, popped mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Sauté onion and chilli
steps.text: Add the onion and green chilli and sauté for 3 minutes until soft and just starting to colour. Stir in the turmeric.
steps.visual: Soft, lightly golden onion and green chilli tinged yellow with turmeric in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Lower the heat and pour in the eggs. Let them set for 20 seconds, then stir and break them into small, soft curds for 2 to 3 minutes. Stop while they are still moist.
steps.visual: Soft yellow egg curds with onion and curry leaves being broken up with a spatula in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle crushed pepper and coriander and serve hot with rasam rice, chapati or as a breakfast with dosa.
steps.visual: Fluffy yellow egg podimas with onion, curry leaves and coriander on a steel plate, cracked pepper on top, rasam and rice beside

substitutions.note: Use part egg whites for a leaner podimas.
Coconut oil adds a South Indian aroma.

recipes.reheating: Warm briefly in a pan; avoid overcooking.

recipes.title: Paneer Pepper Fry
recipes.description: Chettinad-style dry paneer fry with onion and capsicum, tossed in coconut oil with curry leaves and a freshly roasted, coarsely crushed pepper, fennel and cumin masala.

steps.title: Roast and crush the pepper masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the pepper, fennel and cumin in a kadai on low heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Cool and crush coarsely in a mortar.
steps.visual: Coarsely crushed black pepper, fennel and cumin in a stone mortar with a few whole peppercorns

steps.title: Cut paneer and vegetables
steps.text: Cut the paneer into 1-inch cubes, slice the onion and cut the capsicum into squares of a similar size.
steps.visual: Neat white paneer cubes, sliced onion and green capsicum squares in three piles on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper and sauté
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in the kadai. Add the curry leaves and green chilli, then the onion, and sauté for 2 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and turmeric and cook for a minute.
steps.visual: Softened onion slices, crackling curry leaves and slit green chilli with yellow ginger-garlic paste in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Add the capsicum
steps.text: Add the capsicum and stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes so it stays crunchy.
steps.visual: Bright green capsicum squares blistering with the onions in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss the paneer
steps.text: Add the paneer, salt and the crushed pepper masala. Toss gently on medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the paneer is hot and coated. Don't overcook or it will harden.
steps.visual: Paneer cubes coated in coarse black pepper masala with capsicum, onion and curry leaves in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot with chapati, dosa or a bowl of rasam.
steps.visual: Peppery paneer fry with capsicum and curry leaves heaped on a white plate, garnished with coriander

substitutions.note: Pressed firm tofu makes it vegan.
Gingelly oil gives a more Chettinad flavour.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes; microwaving toughens paneer.

recipes.title: Air-Fryer Cauliflower 65
recipes.description: Chennai's favourite spicy fried snack made lighter in the air fryer: cauliflower florets in a red chilli, ginger-garlic and curd coating, tossed with fried curry leaves and green chillies.

steps.title: Blanch the florets
steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan with a pinch of salt. Add the florets for 3 minutes, then drain and spread on a towel to steam-dry completely.
steps.visual: Blanched white cauliflower florets spread out to dry on a kitchen towel, a steaming steel saucepan behind

steps.title: Mix the coating
steps.text: In a bowl mix the curd, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste. Stir in the besan and cornflour.
steps.visual: A thick, bright red spiced batter in a steel mixing bowl with a spoon

steps.title: Coat and rest
steps.text: Add the dry florets and toss until each one is evenly coated. Drizzle over half the oil, toss again and rest for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Cauliflower florets thickly coated in red masala in the steel mixing bowl, glistening with a little oil

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Arrange the florets in a single layer in the air-fryer basket. Air-fry at 190°C for 15 to 16 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and charred at the edges. In an oven, bake at 220°C for 20 to 25 minutes on a lined tray, turning once.
steps.visual: Crisp, deep red cauliflower florets with charred edges in an open air-fryer basket

steps.title: Fry the curry leaves
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a small kadai, add the curry leaves and green chillies and fry for 30 seconds until crisp.
steps.visual: Crisp, dark green curry leaves and blistered slit green chillies in a little oil in a small black kadai

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Tip the hot cauliflower into the kadai, toss with the curry leaves and chillies and serve immediately with a squeeze of lemon.
steps.visual: Crisp red cauliflower 65 heaped on a plate with fried curry leaves and green chillies, lemon wedges and onion rings beside

substitutions.note: Use all besan for a gluten-free, slightly higher-protein coating.
Skip the curd and use more lemon juice for a vegan coating.

recipes.storage: Best eaten immediately; it softens on standing.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in the air fryer at 180°C for 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Kondakadalai Sundal
recipes.description: Brown chickpeas boiled until tender and tossed in a coconut-oil tempering of mustard, urad dal, red chilli and curry leaves with fresh coconut. A Navaratri and beach-side favourite.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Wash the chickpeas and soak them in plenty of water for 8 hours or overnight.
steps.visual: Plump brown chickpeas soaked overnight in a steel bowl of water

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Drain and pressure-cook the chickpeas with fresh water and the salt for 5 to 6 whistles, about 20 minutes, until tender but not mushy. Drain well.
steps.visual: Tender, whole brown chickpeas drained in a steel colander, steam rising

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they pop add urad dal, red chillies, hing and curry leaves and fry until the dal is golden.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden urad dal, red chilli pieces and curry leaves in coconut oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss the chickpeas
steps.text: Add the drained chickpeas and toss for 2 minutes so they absorb the tempering. Turn off the heat and mix in the grated coconut.
steps.visual: Brown chickpeas tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves and white grated coconut in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm in small bowls or paper cones as an evening snack.
steps.visual: Kondakadalai sundal in a small steel bowl and a paper cone, flecked with coconut, curry leaves and red chilli

substitutions.note: White chickpeas (vellai kondakadalai) work the same way.
Use gluten-free hing if needed.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan for 1 to 2 minutes, or eat at room temperature.

recipes.title: Pasi Paruppu Sundal
recipes.description: A light, quick sundal of soaked moong dal cooked just tender and tossed with a green chilli, ginger and mustard tempering, grated carrot, coconut and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.title: Soak the dal
steps.text: Wash the moong dal and soak it in water for 1 hour.
steps.visual: Yellow moong dal soaking in water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Cook until just tender
steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan with the salt. Add the drained dal and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until just tender but still whole — taste often, it turns mushy quickly. Drain at once.
steps.visual: Just-cooked, whole yellow moong dal grains in a steel strainer, steam rising

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai, add the mustard seeds and let them pop. Add green chilli, ginger, hing and curry leaves and stir for 20 seconds.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, chopped green chilli, ginger and curry leaves sizzling in oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss everything
steps.text: Add the drained dal and toss gently for 1 minute. Turn off the heat and fold in the carrot, coconut and lemon juice.
steps.visual: Yellow moong dal tossed with orange grated carrot, white coconut, curry leaves and mustard seeds in the black iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature as a snack or light breakfast.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of bright yellow pasi paruppu sundal with orange carrot, coconut and curry leaves

substitutions.note: Finely chopped cucumber adds crunch; raw mango is traditional in summer.
Use gluten-free hing if needed.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Eat at room temperature or warm briefly in a pan.

recipes.title: Verkadalai Sundal (Peanut Sundal)
